title: Quarter-hour clock-boundary predictability (periodic algorithmic trading)
economic_hypothesis: Algorithmic execution is scheduled on calendar-time bar boundaries, so order flow and volatility burst at minute, five-minute and quarter-hour marks. Boundary order imbalance should therefore carry information about subsequent returns, and boundary returns should be partly forecastable from their own boundary-aligned lags.
market: Binance USDT perpetual futures (source); spot BTC/ETH would be the runtime proxy
entry_rules: UNKNOWN as an entry/exit rule. The source provides forecasting regressions: quarter-hour opening 10-second return predictable out of sample from boundary-aligned lags plus technical indicators; quarter-hour opening order imbalance predicts returns over 4 to 12 hours.
parameters: Clock phase (minute/five-minute/quarter-hour) and lags are the functional parameters; no trading thresholds, no sizing.
claimed_metrics: out-of-sample predictability of quarter-hour opening returns; horizon-specific regressions showing predictive content concentrated at the quarter-hour frequency and at 4-12 hour horizons; no return, Sharpe or cost-adjusted figure
required_data: Binance aggregate trade data (public archive); spot OHLCV for the runtime
external_results: High-quality, recent working paper; the authors acknowledge an independent data-validation and replication study by a third party. The evidence is strong about a microstructure regularity and silent about economics after costs.
counter_evidence: The documented object is a 10-second opening return forecast: its magnitude is far below the project's 23.791 bps round-trip cost floor, and the runtime decides on a 15-minute cadence, not 10 seconds.

The 4-12 hour order-imbalance channel is order flow again: the project has already tested tick-level flow imbalance internally and cost-killed it (gross +0.48 to +0.61 bps against a 23.791 bps round trip).
The source studies perpetual futures, while the runtime is spot-only; the spot venue's boundary structure is not the object of the paper.
Any tick-level boundary execution requires infrastructure the project deliberately does not run.
ambiguities: No tradable rule, no cost model, no expected magnitude per trade.
Whether the effect survives on spot venues at all is untested by the source.
replication_difficulty: HIGH (execution cadence and cost headroom), despite excellent data availability.
evidence_quality: HIGH as market microstructure evidence; NOT an economic claim.
overfitting_risk: MEDIUM (many clock phases and lags are testable)
selection_note: The best-evidenced source in the registry, and still rejected: an effect measured in fractions of a basis point on a 10-second horizon cannot be harvested by a spot runtime paying 23.791 bps per round trip on a 15-minute cadence. Evidence quality does not create headroom.
